newsitem.title: USA: CORUS charges off loans connected to probe.
newsitem.headline: CORUS charges off loans connected to probe.

text.p: CORUS Bankshares Inc said Tuesday it charged off $4 million in student loans in the fourth quarter that were subject to an agreement with the U.S. Department of Education.
CORUS said it believes the department has expanded an investigaiton to review whether the bank's student loans division engaged in improper practices from 1988 to April 1994.

As part of an interim agreement with the department, CORUS will not request payment from any guarantor or the department for loans it is not sure were not affected by incorrect servicing history documentation.
The $2.22 billion asset bank holding company has said previously it discovered former employees falsified some loan servicing records from late 1993 to April 1994.
In addition to the $4 million in charge offs, there were $6.7 million in nonaccural student loans subject to the agreement, CORUS said.
Earlier Tuesday, CORUS reported net income of $10.8 million, or $0.72 a share, in the fourth quarter, compared to $10.0 million, or $0.66 a share a year ago.
CORUS shares were down 1/2 at 32-3/4 Tuesday.
